description: Library and command-line utility for rendering projects templates.

sources.entry: copier - A library and command-line utility for rendering project templates.

summary.one_liner: Copier is a Python library and CLI that renders project templates from local paths or Git URLs, substituting values into files and generating projects from them.
summary.what_it_does: Copier generates new projects from a template directory or Git repository, using a questionnaire defined in copier.yml to collect answers. Templates can contain files and folders with templated names, and Copier can substitute values into any kind of text file. It avoids overwriting existing files unless told to. The README also describes a template-update lifecycle, where consumers can evolve projects when the template changes, though it notes not all templates support updating. Usage is available as the `copier copy` command or as the `run_copy` function in Python. The `gh:` and `gl:` prefixes shortcut GitHub and GitLab repository URLs.
use_cases: scaffold a new Python project from a reusable template
generate project boilerplate from a Git repository
share a project template with a team
update an existing project when its template changes
render templated files and folders from user answers
automate repetitive project setup in scripts
how_to_run: Install Python 3.10 or newer and Git 2.27 or newer
pipx install copier   (or: uv tool install copier)
pip install copier   (or: conda install -c conda-forge copier)
brew install copier   (Homebrew formula for macOS or Linux)
summary.notable:
["Works with both local template paths and Git URLs, with gh: and gl: shortcuts", "Questionnaire defined in copier.yml that collects answers used during rendering", "Answers are recorded in a file so templates can be updated later", "Usable as both a command-line tool and a Python library", "Templates are discoverable via the copier-template GitHub topic"]</notable>
<parameter name="caveats">["Requires Python 3.10+ and Git 2.27+ to be installed", "Not all templates support updating after generation", "Uses Git for template sources, so remote templates need Git access"]
